walkthroughs.body_html:
Numbers & The Number System — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Numbers & The Number System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Numbers & The Number System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of the mixed number 2 1/3?
options: 3/7 — first convert to the improper fraction 7/3, then flip it.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
(-3)^2 equals -6 because the negative makes you subtract.
1/2 1/3, by flipping each part of the mixed number separately.
(-3)^2 equals -9 because the minus is preserved.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
9 — squaring a negative gives a positive.
(-3)^2 equals -6 because the negative makes you subtract.
2 — subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so -3 + 5 = 2.
-2 1/3, because reciprocal means 'opposite'.
-15, because two negatives multiply to give a larger negative result.
-8, because two negatives combine to make a bigger negative.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rational number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Square number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cube number”?
options: Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prime number”?
options: A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Irrational number”?
options: Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Integer”?
options: Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
